text:
alert-bot: [ALERT] GPU pool saturation: region-us-east-1/gpu-pool-4 at 98% and queue length 12k, 429s increasing
lee: I'm on it, picking up pager. marking as P0
maria: seeing same in telemetry, 5m spike in enqueue latency, token bucket rejects increasing from 0.2%->12%
sam: any customer impact yet?
cs-rep: noticing multiple customers reporting timeouts in PROD through support — one enterprise job failed repeatedly, escalated
lee: throughput drop due to autoscaler failing to add new instances. I see autoscaler stuck at desired=10, max=10. check config
jordan: looks like a recent ratepolicy rollout 2h ago lowered burst tokens for tier 'standard' in us-east — could be causing backpressure
maria: confirm: token refill rate for standard was decreased 30% by rollout 2024-11-02T14:05; that reduces effective concurrency on hotpath
sre-rotation: oncall, please coordinate with runtime to raise max and adjust tokenbucket while we stabilize
oncall-bot: @sre-rotation acknowledged; created incident INC-2024-453, channel pinned
lee: running quick mitigation: increase autoscaler max to 20, giving headroom. running:
```
# internal admin
infractl autoscaler update --pool gpu-pool-4 --max-instances 20
```
maria: also temporarily reverting ratepolicy change for 'standard' in us-east to previous burst/refill values
sam: advise: if we increase autoscaler but tokenbucket still tight, queue will still pile because requests get rejected early. need both
jordan: rolling back ratepolicy now
```
# runtime config rollback
runtimectl ratepolicy set --name standard --region us-east --burst 2000 --refill 400
```
lee: autoscaler accepted new max, but new nodes are provisioning slowly. node add rate limited by cloud quotas, ETA ~6m
maria: deployed tokenbucket rollback, testing with load replay on staging to validate. will tail logs.
eng-runtime-bot: GPU pool 4 utilization: 100% -> 88% after scaling hint; queue length dropping from 12k -> 4.2k
cs-rep: started triage with affected customer, letting them know mitigation in progress :phone: 
lee: also temporarily relaxing tier routing to allow 'standard' traffic to fall back to 'burst' tier while we stabilize. doing config flip:
```
routingctl set-fallback --from standard --to burst --region us-east --enable
```
maria: monitoring error rate: 429s dropped from 34% -> 9% in 3m
sre-rotation: great. next steps: 1) keep autoscaler max at 20 for 1h 2) revert routing fallback after queue <500 3) create postmortem to explain ratepolicy rollout regression
sam: logging actions for follow-up, assigning postmortem to maria + lee + runtime eng
kate: Heads-up: open PR for ratepolicy should include load-tests and a tuned tokenbucket plan before rollout
lee: agree. I'll update the incident channel when queue <500 or if anything regresses
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2024-453 sev -> mitigated, will remain P1 for monitoring
maria: last check: queue 380, 429s at 1.4%, GPU util 68% — marking as stabilized
cs-rep: notified customers of mitigation and timeline, they acknowledged :white_check_mark:
lee: thanks all. follow-up action items: postmortem, stricter rollout gating for ratepolicy, increase cloud quota for faster node provisioning
sam: closing handoff to next oncall in 30m, will document runbook additions
lee: handing off to @sre-rotation for overnight watch
sre-rotation: taking over, reading logs, will alert if regression detected
